shapes.name: Trigger
shapes.doc: CanonicalLorebook - the world-info / knowledge-base entity. Adopts the RoleCall LorebookEntry as the canonical baseline (it is a practical superset of SillyTavern World Info, Risu, Agnai, Chub, Lumiverse, and NovelAI's portable surface). Field map + cross-format coverage in design/LOREBOOK-FORMATS.md and specs/formats/rolecall-lorebook.md. Only PORTABLE format content is first-classed here. RC's DB/platform baggage (creator, stats, publishing status, fork lineage, versioning, timestamps, token counts, per-session runtime state) is NOT part of the canonical body - it rides in original or on the Entity wrapper, exactly as the character body strips its DB fields. A character references lorebooks by id via CharacterBody.knowledgeRefs (ordered); a format that must embed the book resolves those on export. The wire gate still holds: a field earns a first-class slot only if some real WIRE format SERIALIZES it. RC in-memory-only fields with no serializer producer (allowRecursion, boostIds, boostAmount, scanPreset, probabilityMode - verified absent from packages/lorebook serializeEntryToRoleCallV1 + the ST serializer) ride original: first-classing a field nothing serializes is dead surface. But under the schema-is-editor doctrine, an AUTHORED field a real format DOES serialize gets a slot even if only one format produces it (single-platform is not a reason to original). So ST's extra scan sources (matchCharacterDepthPrompt, matchCreatorNotes), the vectorized/group-override/group-scoring toggles, the automation binding, and the distinct displayIndex axis are first-classed below - they are ST wire fields a creator sets, not in-memory residue. A keyword/regex trigger. "Advanced" triggers carry their own `probability` (overriding the entry fallback); "simple" triggers omit it and use the entry-level probability. `frequency` is config (min messages between activations); per-session runtime counters are not part of portable content.

fields.name: flags
fields.meaning: regex flags: g, i, m, s, u, y

fields.name: frequency
fields.meaning: min messages that must pass before this trigger can re-activate its entry

fields.name: probability
fields.meaning: advanced mode only: per-trigger activation chance 0-100, overrides the entry fallback

shapes.name: CharacterFilter
shapes.doc: Whitelist (isExclude:false) or blacklist (isExclude:true) an entry to specific characters.

shapes.name: EntrySideEffect
shapes.doc: A variable mutation performed when an entry activates (declarative data, never executed by vaud).

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: for setvar

fields.name: amount
fields.meaning: for addvar/incvar/decvar

shapes.name: EntryContextConfig
shapes.doc: NovelAI per-entry context-assembly config: authored prompt-shaping dials a creator sets in the NAI lorebook UI (prefix/suffix are authored TEXT, e.g. "[ Mal: " / " ]\n"). All optional; formats without an assembly layer omit the whole block. NAI's `budgetPriority` is deliberately NOT here - it is the placement axis and lives in `sortOrder` (one home per axis, see the sortOrder/priority split below).

fields.name: prefix
fields.meaning: text prepended to the entry when inserted

fields.name: suffix
fields.meaning: text appended to the entry when inserted

fields.name: tokenBudget
fields.meaning: per-entry token budget cap

fields.name: reservedTokens
fields.meaning: tokens reserved so the entry is not trimmed away

fields.name: trimDirection
fields.meaning: trim strategy: "doNotTrim" | "trimBottom" | "trimTop" (open: NAI may add values)

fields.name: insertionType
fields.meaning: join strategy: "newline" | "space" | "token"

fields.name: maximumTrimType
fields.meaning: trim granularity: "sentence" | "newline" | "token"

fields.name: insertionPosition
fields.meaning: signed offset within the target context section (NOT canonical depth - a different axis)

shapes.name: LoreBiasPhrase
shapes.doc: One phrase inside a NovelAI loreBiasGroups row. Wire uses `sequence` and/or `sequences` plus a numeric `type` (NAI's phrase-type enum). Authored content - first-class so the editor can edit bias.

fields.name: type
fields.meaning: NAI phrase type (int on wire; open enum)

shapes.name: LoreBiasGroup
shapes.doc: NovelAI phrase-bias group: signed bias applied when the entry is active (or when inactive if `whenInactive`). Ported from real v3/v6 exports (loreBiasGroups).

fields.name: bias
fields.meaning: signed strength (e.g. -0.5, 0.2)

fields.name: id
fields.meaning: stable entry id, preserved across round-trips (categories reference it)

fields.name: title
fields.meaning: entry label (maps to ST `comment`)

fields.name: comment
fields.meaning: internal creator note; distinct from title, has no ST home (RC-only)

fields.name: constant
fields.meaning: always inject regardless of keyword match

fields.name: caseSensitive
fields.meaning: null = inherit the lorebook global

fields.name: depth
fields.meaning: used when position is "depth" or "append"

fields.name: sortOrder
fields.meaning: Placement / insertion order: where the entry lands relative to its siblings in the assembled prompt. The universal ordering axis - ST `order`, Risu `insertorder`, CCv3 `insertion_order`, Agnai `weight`, RC `sortOrder`. (ST's cosmetic `displayIndex` is a distinct display axis with only one source format, so it rides original, not a canonical slot.)

fields.name: priority
fields.meaning: Eviction / budget priority: which entries survive when the token budget is exceeded (higher survives). A separate axis from placement - CCv3 `priority`, Agnai `priority`, RC `priority`. Formats with no eviction field (ST, Risu) default this to 100.

fields.name: categoryId
fields.meaning: references a LorebookCategory.id

fields.name: probability
fields.meaning: entry-level activation chance 0-100 (fallback for simple triggers)

fields.name: excludeRecursion
fields.meaning: will NOT be found during recursion (direct matches only)

fields.name: preventRecursion
fields.meaning: this entry's content will NOT trigger other entries

fields.name: delayUntilRecursion
fields.meaning: only activate at recursion level N (0 = first pass)

fields.name: scanCharacterDepthPrompt
fields.meaning: extra ST worldinfo scan sources (undefined = not produced by this format / off)

fields.name: ignoreBudget
fields.meaning: bypass token budget - always inject

fields.name: vectorized
fields.meaning: Authored ST-lineage entry toggles that only some formats carry (optional: undefined = the format has no such field, distinct from an explicit false a producer set). First-classed per the schema-is-editor doctrine, not original. `vectorized` is the RAG toggle (the SETTING, not the vectors, which stay original); `groupOverride`/`useGroupScoring` extend the groupName/groupWeight mutual-exclusion axis; `automationId` binds an entry to a Quick-Reply automation by id (the id only, the automation set stays original).

fields.name: keyRelative
fields.meaning: NovelAI: keys match relative to the entry's own insertion point, not the story tail

fields.name: nonStoryActivatable
fields.meaning: NovelAI: entry can activate outside story text (e.g. from a UI action)

fields.name: contextConfig
fields.meaning: NovelAI authored per-entry assembly config (prefix/suffix/trim/budget dials)

fields.name: loreBiasGroups
fields.meaning: NovelAI phrase bias groups (loreBiasGroups on wire)

fields.name: displayIndex
fields.meaning: Creator's manual display order in the editor list - a DISTINCT authored axis from `sortOrder` (placement in the assembled prompt). Real ST cards prove they diverge (Seraphina: sortOrder all 100, displayIndex 0-3), so it is NOT regenerable from sortOrder. null/undefined = follow sortOrder.

fields.name: metadata
fields.meaning: extensible bag for format-specific data with no first-class home

shapes.name: LorebookCategory
shapes.doc: A folder grouping entries within a lorebook.

fields.name: enabled
fields.meaning: Book-level on/off for the shelf + Press export filter. Default true when absent (older books). RC can round-trip it; other formats ignore (deny by absence).

fields.name: globalCaseSensitive
fields.meaning: global matching defaults; entries with null matching options inherit these
